clue.text: College film about Georgia John Smith?

indicators.note: college and film together sit about, that is around, the state's abbreviation

parts.note: POLY is short for polytechnic, a kind of college
a film of moisture is a mist
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A college made a film about the state of Georgia featuring someone called John Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, with college and film wrapped round the state. The question mark warns that John Smith is only an example, an everyman name like those of early Mormons who took several wives.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks an example: a man with several wives at once, as some early Mormon leaders named Smith had.

clue.text: Power ballad that 4 has written before?

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad

explanation.surface: A power ballad that the playwright had composed earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is the answer to 4-down, the playwright David Mamet, so the definition asks for something he has written.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamet is a dramatist, so his written works are stage dramas.

clue.text: Those heading left over road with daughter to see Macbeth?

indicators.note: the letters at the head of each of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: People leading the way left across a road with a girl to visit Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, a Scottish nobleman, hence the question mark for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is an example of a Scottish nobleman, a thane and peer of the realm.

clue.text: Cur upset with success at Sanditon's author's peak

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for cur is turned upside down

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to succeed is to win
Sanditon is the unfinished last novel of Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A dog knocked over after a win at the mountain named for the author of Sanditon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DOG to GOD. Godwin-Austen is another name for K2, the world's second-highest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Godwin-Austen is an alternative name for K2, the Himalayan mountain summit.

clue.text: In the morning, police force to arrest Pulitzer winner

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the police force word holds the morning abbreviation

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: At dawn the police move in to arrest a prize-winning author.
explanation.definitionFit: David Mamet won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama for Glengarry Glen Ross.

clue.text: French wines ruined NHS careers, but not hospital

indicators.note: ruined says the remaining letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
but not tells us to drop a letter from the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Health-service careers wrecked, though hospitals themselves are spared, leading to French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes H from NHSCAREERS, leaving NSCAREERS, which 'ruined' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a white wine from the Loire valley; the plural means bottles of it.

clue.text: French main and cold starter for Cat Shannon?

parts.note: the main is the sea, which in French is mer

indicators.note: the starter of the word cold is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A French main course with a cold starter for someone called Cat Shannon.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat Shannon is the soldier of fortune who leads the hired fighters in Frederick Forsyth's The Dogs of War.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is informal shorthand for a mercenary, a soldier for hire like Forsyth's hero.

clue.text: Limping chap who's very quiet since cutting gas

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the word for since goes inside the gas

parts.note: ethane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas
since, as in 'since Monday', means from

explanation.surface: A hobbling, silent man has been around ever since the gas was cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is the container signal. Edith Wharton's title character is a taciturn farmer left lame by a sledging accident, so the definition covers both his limp and his silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharton's title character is a crippled, taciturn New England farmer.

clue.text: Tea and energy-packed fruit for folk like Tartuffe

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: packed means filled, so the fruit has the energy symbol packed inside it

parts.note: melons are fruit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Tea and fruit full of energy for people such as Moliere's Tartuffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed' puts E inside MELONS. Tartuffe, in Moliere's play, is a hypocrite who changes his face to suit his company.
explanation.definitionFit: People who change their opinions or manner to suit circumstances are likened to lizards that change colour.

clue.text: "Here lies David Garrick, describe me who can, / An — of all that was pleasant in man" (Oliver Goldsmith)

definitions.text: "Here lies David Garrick, describe me who can, / An — of all that was pleasant in man" (Oliver Goldsmith)

parts.words: "Here lies David Garrick, describe me who can, / An — of all that was pleasant in man" (Oliver Goldsmith)
parts.note: fill the gap in Goldsmith's mock epitaph on the actor Garrick from his poem Retaliation

explanation.surface: A quotation from Goldsmith's poem Retaliation with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the solution, an old spelling without the E after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitaph calls Garrick a condensed version, a shortened summary, of all that was pleasant in mankind.

clue.text: Goddess content in designer headdress

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the answer is contained in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A goddess wears what a designer has put into a headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the Titaness of Greek myth, mother of Zeus and other Olympians.

clue.text: Doctor and corporal, perhaps, in wetland vessel

indicators.note: in places the military word inside the wetland word

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
corporal is an example of a military rank
a stein is a beer mug, a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A doctor and an army corporal are aboard a boat in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Shelley's Victor is a student of natural science rather than a medical man, but popular culture always calls him Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's scientist Victor Frankenstein is popularly known as Doctor Frankenstein.

clue.text: Royal who questions unimportant photos in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: unimportant means little and photos are prints

explanation.surface: A royal asks about some trivial photographs at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint-Exupery's Little Prince keeps asking questions and never lets one go until it is answered.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Exupery's young hero is a prince from an asteroid who keeps asking the narrator questions.

clue.text: Nobel winner left area to climb frost-topped mountain

indicators.note: topped means the frost word sits on top of the mountain word in this down entry
in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so these letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: frost is ice crystals
a Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet high

explanation.surface: A Nobel laureate left the district to climb a mountain capped with frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns LA into AL. A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, named after Sir Hugh Munro who listed them.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Munro, the Canadian short-story writer, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2013.

clue.text: Governess who wrote Eton banner for a new display

indicators.note: a new display of the letters means arranging them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A governess-author writes a banner for Eton to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Bronte was a governess herself and wrote Agnes Grey, a novel about one.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest Bronte sister worked as a private tutor in families before writing novels.

clue.text: Network with one choosing actors for Shakespearean role

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network
someone who casts a play chooses its actors

explanation.surface: A network and a casting director choose actors for a Shakespeare part.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, appears in Richard II; other Lancasters appear in the Henry IV plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes of Lancaster are characters in Shakespeare's history plays such as Richard II.

clue.text: "The counsellor heart, the arm our soldier, / Our steed the leg, the tongue our —" (Coriolanus)

definitions.text: "The counsellor heart, the arm our soldier, / Our steed the leg, the tongue our —" (Coriolanus)

parts.words: "The counsellor heart, the arm our soldier, / Our steed the leg, the tongue our —" (Coriolanus)
parts.note: fill the gap in the citizen's speech comparing parts of the body to members of the state

explanation.surface: A quotation from Coriolanus with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the fable of the belly in Act 1 of Coriolanus.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue proclaims things as a herald who sounds a horn does.

clue.text: Duckett's job is head of new employment, Republican claimed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
claimed means taken in, so the employment word takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: Someone's job is head of new employment, a Republican asserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claimed' puts R inside USE. Nurse Duckett is a character in Joseph Heller's Catch-22.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue Ann Duckett in Catch-22 works in the hospital as a carer for the sick.

clue.text: Sort of problems Valentinov created in revolutionary guard?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard

explanation.surface: Puzzles made by someone inside a revolutionary guard unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Valentinov, in Nabokov's The Defence, is the manager who exploits the prodigy Luzhin and composes such problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed board-game puzzles such as mate-in-two are a genre of their own, set by specialists.

clue.text: One such as Seamus Heaney turns male off

indicators.note: off means awry or gone wrong, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet turns the man away.
explanation.walkthrough: Heaney was born in County Londonderry, in the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaney came from Northern Ireland, whose historic province gives its natives that name.

clue.text: Criminal male corrupts writer obsessed with memory

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the following letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked man corrupts a writer obsessed with remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust's In Search of Lost Time grows from involuntary memory, the famous madeleine dipped in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Proust's great novel is built on recollection of the past triggered by sensations.

clue.text: Monsters turn up on holiday? Time to leave!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a turn in a game is your go

indicators.note: to leave means the time abbreviation departs from the holiday word

parts.note: a holiday is a rest

explanation.surface: Monsters turn up while you are on holiday, so it is time to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the go upside down in this down entry, and 'to leave' drops the time letter from the holiday word; 'on' means one piece sits on top of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, the classic monsters of fairy tales.

parts.note: a handbook is a guide

explanation.walkthrough: Andre Gide was associated with the Symbolist movement early in his career.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide began writing among the French Symbolist poets in the 1890s.

clue.text: Parts of a book initially expurgated in Times

explanation.definitionFit: Ages are long periods or eras, as in 'the Victorian age'.

clue.text: Two articles written about French tart

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the second copy of the indefinite article
